extra.message: GET /api/v2/user passes the raw, attacker-controlled query parameter req.query.name directly into eval(): `res.send('Welcome name ' + eval(req.query.name));`. This allows arbitrary server-side JavaScript execution (RCE) — e.g. ?name=require('child_process').execSync('id') — since eval() runs on the Node.js server with full process privileges.

cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection')

extra.message: The /contact route reads the user-controlled `url` query parameter (parsed from req.url at lines 190-191) and passes it directly to needle.get(query.url, ...). An attacker can make the server send arbitrary HTTP(S) requests to internal services (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/ cloud metadata, http://localhost:<port>), i.e. SSRF.

cwe: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)

extra.message: After the needle.get() probe succeeds, the handler calls res.redirect(query.url) where query.url is fully attacker-controlled. An attacker can supply ?url=https://evil.example and this trusted origin will issue an HTTP redirect to it, enabling phishing/credential theft (open redirect).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: GET /api/v1/users/:name is registered WITHOUT the auth middleware and returns the full profile document (name, email, age, _id) of any user looked up by name (User.findOne({name: name}) at line 244). This exposes every user's PII without authentication and enables user enumeration plus ID harvesting that feeds the token-forgery and IDOR flaws.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: GET /api/v1/tasks has no auth middleware and returns Task.find({}) — i.e. every task belonging to every user (descriptions, completion state and owner ObjectIds) to any unauthenticated caller. This is a cross-tenant information disclosure.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: PATCH /api/v1/users/:id (line 281) only checks that the caller is authenticated; it then does User.findById(req.params.id) with NO check that the target belongs to the caller and writes arbitrary whitelisted fields (name/email/password/age) onto the target. Any authenticated user can change another user's email/password, achieving full account takeover. The attacker only needs the victim's _id, obtainable from the unauthenticated /api/v1/users/:name endpoint.

extra.message: DELETE /api/v1/users/:id (route at line 306) is protected only by authentication, not authorization: User.findByIdAndDelete(req.params.id) removes the account identified by the user-supplied :id. Any authenticated user can delete any other user's account (denial of service / destruction of data).

Any logged-in user can modify (description/completed) any other user's task. The `s` typo on line 43 is unrelated dead syntax.

extra.message: POST /api/v2/profile takes the entire attacker-controlled object req.body.profile and passes it as the render context: res.render('profile', profile). profile.hbs includes the header partial ({{> header}}), and header.hbs contains the UNESCAPED `{{{body}}}` tag (public/templates/partials/header.hbs:39). Because the partial inherits the attacker-supplied context, sending {"profile":{"body":"<script>...</script>"}} injects arbitrary HTML/JS into the server-rendered response.

extra.message: The session JWT is set with res.cookie('auth_token', token) (also line 36 for login) without httpOnly, Secure, or SameSite attributes. The token cookie is therefore readable by JavaScript — confirmed by public/js/client-app.js:6 and profile-app.js, which read document.cookie — so any XSS (or a network eavesdropper, since Secure is absent) can steal the session token.

extra.message: The JWT verification secret is hardcoded as the string 'hardsecret' (shared, publicly visible in source). Anyone who knows it can forge valid-looking tokens for any user _id (used with the predictable-signature generation in src/models/user.js:71), defeating the signature check of the authentication middleware.

extra.message: Auth tokens are signed with the hardcoded secret jwt.sign({ _id: user._id.toString() }, 'hardsecret'). The static, source-visible signing key lets an attacker reproduce the token stream and, combined with the predictable payload, weaken the entire session scheme (see matching hardcoded verify secret in src/middleware/auth.js:8).
